title: fix(ui): release Markdown workers in hidden tabs
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Long code blocks can keep syntax-highlighting workers and Markdown observers active after their browser tab becomes hidden.

## User Impact

Hidden tabs release pending syntax workers and foreground observers across transcripts, Markdown attachments, and Custodian. Returning resumes unfinished highlighting for presented panes, preserving complete code text and controls.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared `MarkdownBlocks` owner composes document visibility with caller presentation intent using the existing shared subscription. A tab reveal cannot reactivate a pane the caller parked. Disposal releases the subscription. Worker cancellation and source retention remain with their existing owners.

ClawSweeper identified that the first ref-level gate missed attachment and Custodian owners. This revision moves the gate into the shared owner and removes the adapter policy.

## Evidence

- Hidden and visible mounts; observers released on hide; repeated Custodian-style publications while hidden; pane gating; queued scan fenced by disposal.
- Real attachment panel mounted alongside a transcript: both share one syntax worker, hide terminates it once, reveal restarts both, and disposing the attachment leaves only the transcript consumer. Source and node identity stay intact.
- Four direct/mixed-consumer regressions fail against the original ref-only producer, then pass with the owner repair.
- CI exposed two attachment-refresh browser regressions in the first shared-owner revision. Native Chromium reproduced both; the original owner passed all seven cases. Solid creates replacement refs in an inert template document before adoption, so visibility must follow the ambient rendering document. Both reads and subscription now use that document, as the installed Solid contract requires.
- A new template-adoption regression fails against the previous head and passes with this correction; it covers activation before adoption, real-tab visibility delivery, retained source and disposal. All seven existing attachment Chromium cases and 72 focused tests now pass.
- Targeted formatting, lint, UI type checking, the test-lines ratchet, and `git diff --check` pass. No CPU or heap benchmark is claimed.
- Production delta: +14 lines; tests: +230 lines. The positive production delta establishes the shared owner boundary for all three callers; no new framework or configuration.
- Independent local corrective review is scoped-clean through P2. The [exact-head hosted review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/187691#issuecomment-6498838120) at `1aa6960b960243319489bd5bdce5b44097adb344` reports no findings or pre-merge requests. [Fresh full CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40893755071) reports a workspace-search unit failure in `checks-ui (3/3)`; the attachment-refresh shard passes. The earlier attachment-refresh failure is repaired, not treated as inherited.
- Rank-up move: the optional native-worker hide/reveal trace is deferred to a separate performance-proof follow-up. The accepted repair is covered at its shared lifecycle boundary plus real Chromium attachment refresh; no quantitative CPU/heap reduction or native worker trace is claimed here.

## Unrelated CI attribution

The workspace case `desktop browses lazy directories and restores activity after an incomplete search` receives undefined rather than `absent` at `chat-session-workspace-rail.test.tsx:647`. Actual CI merge `2387c847f497765f744c190b74de725a2cb07bba` has ordered parents main `55d82ecb0da219c6e34284f265a19d12884b80a3` and the reviewed PR head. All 22 inspected workspace owner, fixture, harness, shared-primitive and dependency blobs match that actual main parent. The complete merge delta contains only this PR's four Markdown files.

The workspace fixture opens no preview and supplies no transcript attachments. Its search state belongs to the unchanged input/debounce/list owner; the Markdown listener is installed only on construction. The exact fixture also passes with a temporary throwing MarkdownBlocks constructor fence, proving the changed owner is not entered. Added tests retire their owners and restore visibility/global mocks; the unchanged non-isolated runner restores roots, timers, mocks and modules between files. Independent and primary source investigation agree on attribution.

The focused case and original-order full 20-case workspace file pass locally. This supports the causal attribution; it does not make failed CI green or establish a confirmed historical flake. The scoped land instruction selects the native inherited-CI exception after all jobs finish and independent security passes.

Follow-up: reproduce lazy browse → read → rapid query replacement → close → missing → close/reopen → absent in the complete UI shard; inspect the 160ms debounce, close-search read, loading/pendingReload and stale-list finalization together. Keep this separate workspace investigation out of the Markdown visibility repair.
